summary.headline: H1 FY27 turnover ~363 crore vs 380 crore, PAT ~40 crore flat; Q2 PAT fell to ~16 crore as feed raw material costs rose.
summary.overview: Management described H1 FY27 as broadly flat year on year: turnover about 363 crore versus 380 crore, EBITDA about 67-44 crore (transcript reads "6744 crores", unclear) and PAT about 40 crore in both periods. Q2 turnover rose to about 184 crore from 179 crore in Q1, but EBITDA fell to about 28 crore from 38 crore as feed raw material costs increased. Q2 PBT was about 22 crore (32 crore in Q1) and PAT about 16 crore (24 crore in Q1). Management guided to a 100 crore-plus profit for the full year but declined to give quarterly guidance, and the company is in a heavy capex phase funded largely by term debt.

segments.name: Egg powder / egg products
segments.commentary: Powder sales were 1,625 MT in Q2 versus 1,831 MT in Q1, and 3,457 MT in H1 versus 4,289 MT in the prior-year half. Average realisation was cited at about 700 rupees per unit, with management expecting 700-plus in H2 and volumes slightly better.

segments.name: Domestic shell eggs / branded eggs
segments.commentary: Management said it currently sells about 1.5 lakh eggs a day in the branded egg segment and targets 5 lakh eggs a day in two to three years. Business model, segment (premium vs mass) and pricing are still under internal discussion, with a decision expected in about three months.

segments.name: SKM Universal (wholly owned subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Board approved merger of SKM Universal into the listed company; it will cease to exist by April next year. Management said scale-up plans begin in FY28, and a 17.5 crore goodwill-like item in Q2 was described as a share purchase cost from a sister company.

guidance_outlook: Full-year PAT of 100 crore-plus reiterated, described as a ballpark figure; no quarterly guidance given, citing SEBI limits and export volatility.
Next six months expected to continue the past six months with a small margin improvement; more aggressive growth expected from next financial year.
Average realisations not expected to correct significantly over the next six months; Japan pricing reduced due to US oversupply, with pressure elsewhere limited.
Real sales increment from the expanded capacity expected from FY28-FY29; no top-line or bottom-line numbers given.
Dividend payout to be maintained at about 25% even during the high-investment and debt phase.
capex_capacity: EC (layer) farm phase two: 2.4 million birds target by September 28; first rearing house expected complete in about two weeks, chicks to be placed from November 15; project running about one week behind schedule.
Board approved term loan of nearly 300 crore (200 crore State Bank, 100 crore Access Bank); documents to be signed the following week.
Powder capacity expansion from 7,000 to 10,000+ tons at about 180 crore (30 crore margin, about 150 crore term loan at 8.25%), with capacity commissioning around H2 FY28 and 3-5 years to fill.
Management described total debt for the investment phase as about 450 crore.
Cash of about 167 crore held; management said about 100 crore is kept as a minimum for seasonality.
demand_pricing: US oversupply of eggs is reducing prices in Japan; management said pressure elsewhere has been limited and international prices are set by global competitors (Europe, Ukraine, South America, Mexico), not by Indian costs.

Feed raw material (soya and other ingredients) costs rose sharply in Q2; the company cannot fix prices in contracts and has no pass-through mechanism. Management could not confirm pass-through to customers.
Management plans to import soya for about six months of requirement, expected to be about 10% cheaper than local prices; implementation expected in a week or two.
South Korea: two customers have approved samples; bigger trial shipment is under way, with a first order targeted for October-December quarter.
Freight costs rose due to the US-Iran conflict and the Ukraine-Russia war; management said the rupee depreciation offsets part of this and demand has not been affected.

qa_highlights.question: What are realisations outlook for the next six months, and will domestic sales drive growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said US oversupply has hit Japan pricing only; average realisation is about 700 rupees and not expected to correct much. Grading equipment arrives by April, and a relaunch strategy will follow, with the business model still under discussion.

qa_highlights.question: Will profit stay around 100 crore for the year, and can raw material inflation be passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is very confident of repeating 100-plus crore this year. It said international prices are set by global competition, not Indian cost, so pass-through is uncertain; soya imports and backward integration are the offsets.

qa_highlights.question: Will quarterly profits exceed 16 crore in the next two quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give quarterly projections, saying it did not think SEBI permits it, and reiterated only the 100 crore-plus ballpark for the year.

qa_highlights.question: Will the expansion receive interest subvention, and what capex is needed?
qa_highlights.answer: The 3% interest subvention applies only to farm investment, not egg processing. Powder expansion is about 180 crore with 150 crore term loan at 8.25%; benefits from the farms come gradually and fully by September 28.

qa_highlights.question: Why hold about 167 crore cash while borrowing 300 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company keeps about 100 crore for seasonality and that its cost of funds is about 5.25% after 3% interest subvention; it targets returns above 10% on surplus cash.

qa_highlights.question: Will branded domestic eggs become a substantial part of turnover within two to three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects it to become an important revenue stream within two to five years, but segment choice (premium, mid, or mass) is still being decided and should be firmed up in about three months.

risks_watch: Feed cost inflation (soya and other ingredients) compressing EBITDA; Q2 EBITDA fell to about 28 crore from 38 crore.
Japanese price pressure from US oversupply and softening international egg-powder prices.
EC farm commissioning slippage (already about one week behind) and the 2.4 million bird target by September 28.
Debt rising to about 450 crore for the investment phase, with finance costs and dividend policy (25% payout) to watch.
Branded domestic egg strategy and business model still undecided; decision expected in about three months.
Freight cost increases from geopolitical events; South Korea first order targeted October-December.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term growth and the 100-crore-plus full-year profit target, but guarded on quarterly numbers, pass-through of costs, and the timing of the domestic branded egg strategy. Management repeatedly stated that it cannot give quarterly guidance and that the business model is still being worked out.
key_quotes: Yes, we are very confident of repeating 100 plus this year.
So, to be cash surplus in a growth phase is an important criterion than the risk that we have on having a bigger loan.
So, we will try to maintain the 25% even during the high investment phase and the debt period.
So, after all the equipment for grading and will be in place by April next year, we will be relaunching new strategy for growth.

growth.why: Management reiterated FY27 PAT of 100 crore-plus and guided to more aggressive growth from FY28, but gave no top-line numbers; the 3,000+ ton powder expansion (about 180 crore) is commissioning around H2 FY28 and the EC farm phase two is in trial runs, so near-term growth is flat to slightly positive while Q2 EBITDA fell on feed costs.
